meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'говорить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to have a talk', forming an aspectual pair with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Катя, мне нужно с тобой поговорить!

examples.trans: Maybe you will talk with her yourself?

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, можно с вами поговорить?
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, may I speak with you?

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (root 'винить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to excuse', forming an aspectual pair with 'извинять'.

examples.text: Извините, я просто забыл отключить.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I just forgot to turn it off.

examples.text: Извините за опоздание, я уже здесь!
examples.trans: Excuse me for being late, I am here already!

examples.text: Извините, Катя, подожди меня одну секунду!
examples.trans: Excuse me, Katya, wait for me for one second!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (root 'ождать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, you mean Vika in your dream?

examples.text: Подожди, почему твой цветок пахнет виски?
examples.trans: Wait, why does your flower smell like whisky?

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian num meaning 'one', frequent in spoken dialogue.
